record.title: A 66-configuration study reports model–harness ranking reversals across agent tasks
record.summary: Li et al. report 66 model–harness configurations across TUA-Bench, ALE-CLI and a 63-task non-H100 subset of Terminal-Bench 4. Rankings reverse by harness: on the paper’s Terminal-Bench subset, Claude leads GPT-6 Astra by 7.94 points under OpenHands but trails by 30.16 points under PI. GPT-6 Astra scores 60.32% at $4.66 per task under PI versus 52.38% at $19.94 under DeepSeek Harness. The authors release adapters, evaluation code and 6,204 scored trajectories. These are author-reported results from one counted run per task; harness defaults and effective reasoning budgets differ, so the comparison does not isolate a causal harness effect or establish ranking stability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors evaluated 66 model–harness configurations across TUA-Bench, ALE-CLI and a 63-task non-H100 Terminal-Bench 4 subset, and report that model rankings vary by harness and task collection.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent matched multi-run reproduction and ranking uncertainty are unavailable.
The paper uses harness-specific defaults and high-effort labels that may not imply equal reasoning budgets.

brief.importance_rationale: If the measured model–harness interactions generalize, they can change agent system selection and the work delivered per API dollar across common task settings. The study spans 66 configurations and three benchmarks, but one counted run per task and differing harness defaults leave causal attribution and transfer uncertain.
limitations: Results are author-reported; the research desk did not independently rerun the benchmarks or validate provider invoices.
Each task contributes one counted run after reruns; no run-to-run variance or ranking stability is established.
Harness context management, retries, compaction, turn limits and effective reasoning budgets differ; this is not a matched intervention isolating harness causality.
The task subsets and reward conventions are local to this campaign and are not direct reproductions of upstream leaderboard results.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report model ranking reversals across harnesses, task-dependent best harnesses and substantial differences in task score and API cost for the same model.
technical.compute_or_cost: Author-reported OpenRouter API cost per task, including harness auxiliary model calls and excluding evaluator calls.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary paper and its public artifact links exist; the research desk verified the paper text and the reported results table but did not reproduce the experiment.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint with public adapters, evaluation code and scored trajectories; independent reproduction not performed.
technical.mechanism: Crosses five models with four configurable harnesses on three task collections, adding Codex–GPT and Claude Code–Claude native references; compares reward, reported cost and selected trajectories.
technical.regime: 66 configurations on TUA-Bench (120 tasks), ALE-CLI (99 tasks) and a 63-task non-H100 Terminal-Bench 4 subset; one counted run per task after reruns.
technical.reproducibility: Public artifacts are linked by the paper; revisions and independent matched multi-run results still need to be frozen and checked.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-paper matched task identifiers compare harnesses for a given model; the comparison does not equalize all harness defaults or reasoning budgets.

brief.title: A 66-configuration study reports model–harness ranking reversals across agent tasks
brief.why_it_matters: The reported reversals show that model-only rankings may not predict the performance or API cost of a deployed agent configuration. The result supports evaluating model, harness and intended task together, while leaving matched-budget causal effects and repeated-run uncertainty unresolved.
